title: Common lower colimit rank and upper strong accessibility rank
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; all smallness is relative to it and all categories have small Hom sets. Colimits have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. An infinite cardinal $\eta$ is regular when unions of fewer than $\eta$ sets each of size less than $\eta$ have size less than $\eta$. A category is $\eta$-filtered when every diagram with fewer than $\eta$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\eta$-presentable when its Hom functor preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits. A category is $\eta$-accessible when it admits these colimits and has a small family of $\eta$-presentable objects generating it under these colimits; accessible means $\eta$-accessible for some infinite regular $\eta$. A functor is accessible when it preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits for some such $\eta$ for which its source has these colimits.

Let $(\mathcal A_s)_{s\in S}$ be a small family of accessible ordinary categories, and let $(H_t:\mathcal A_{a(t)}\to\mathcal A_{b(t)})_{t\in T}$ be a small family of accessible functors between members of that family. For every small cardinal $b$ there exist infinite regular cardinals $\lambda<\kappa$ in $\mathcal U$, with $b<\kappa$, such that each $\mathcal A_s$ admits all small $\lambda$-filtered colimits and is $\kappa$-accessible, and each $H_t$ preserves all small $\lambda$-filtered and $\kappa$-filtered colimits and takes $\kappa$-presentable objects to $\kappa$-presentable objects. No $\lambda$-accessibility of the categories is asserted.

proof.text:
First establish a rank-enlargement construction with quantified inputs: let $\mathcal C$ be $
u$-accessible, choose its small generating family $G$ of $
u$-presentables, and let $	au>
u$ be infinite regular with $a^d<	au$ for $a<	au,d<
u$. Steps 2-5 prove that $\mathcal C$ is $	au$-accessible and every $	au$-presentable object is a retract of a colimit of a $
u$-filtered diagram in $G$ with fewer than $	au$ arrows. No arbitrary colimits in $\mathcal C$ are assumed.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: state the intermediate claim proved in Steps 2-5; agent expansion of the sharp-rank argument of AR 2.11 and Beke--Rosicky section 3.

proof.text:
For any $X\in\mathcal C$, its defining accessible presentation is a small $
u$-filtered diagram in $G$. Apply [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex] to replace its index by a small $
u$-filtered poset $\Pi$ without changing its colimit cocone; write $F:\Pi	o\mathcal C$ for the resulting diagram. Apply [lem-coef-sharp-filtered-poset-subsets] with $(\alpha, eta,A)=(
u,	au,\Pi)$. Its poset $B$ of $
u$-filtered subsets $J\subseteq\Pi$ of size less than $	au$ is small and $	au$-filtered, including nonemptiness, and covers $\Pi$. Each $J$ is a full subposet, has fewer than $	au$ arrows (a subset of $J	imes J$), and is $
u$-filtered as a category: an upper bound for the fewer than $
u$ vertices of a diagram supplies its cocone. Every arrow of $\Pi$ lies in some $J$, by taking an upper bound in $B$ of members containing its endpoints.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: filtered-poset decomposition, along AR 2.11; the existing sharp-subset node supplies the non-elementary closure argument.

proof.text:
For $J\in B$, let $Q_J=\operatorname{colim}_{J}F|_J$. It exists because $\mathcal C$ admits $
u$-filtered colimits. Every value of $F$ is $	au$-presentable: each $	au$-filtered category is $
u$-filtered, so its Hom comparison is already bijective by $
u$-presentability. Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] to the diagram on $J$, which has fewer than $	au$ arrows, to conclude that $Q_J$ is $	au$-presentable.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: presentability of each small restricted colimit; ordinary Hom version of the AR 2.11 argument.

proof.text: Inclusions $J\subseteq K$ give unique compatible maps $Q_J\to Q_K$; uniqueness proves identities and composition. The resulting cocone $Q\to X$ is colimiting by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: a compatible family $Q_J\to Z$ defines $F(p)\to Z$ using a member containing $p$; a common upper bound of two members proves independence, and a member containing an arrow proves naturality. Conversely a cocone on $F$ restricts to each $J$ and induces a unique compatible family. These operations are inverse. There is a small family containing representatives of all possible $Q_J$, independent of $X$: relabel each $J$ on a cardinal $\delta<\tau$. The poset relations on $\delta$ form a small set, and so do the functors into the fixed small full category on $G$ (its arrows form a small set since $G$ and every Hom set are small). The union over $\delta<\tau$ of these sets is small. Retain the $\nu$-filtered diagrams and choose one colimit of each. Relabelling preserves cocones and their universal properties, so every $Q_J$ is isomorphic to one of these colimits. Replacing values by these representatives and conjugating transition arrows by their isomorphisms preserves the displayed colimit cocone. Thus every $X$ is a small $\tau$-filtered colimit of a fixed small family of $\tau$-presentables. Also $\mathcal C$ admits all $\tau$-filtered colimits, because these are $\nu$-filtered. This proves $\tau$-accessibility.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: explicit cocone gluing and small family of diagrams in a fixed small generator category, completing rank enlargement.

proof.text: If $X=P$ is $\tau$-presentable, the comparison $\operatorname{colim}_{J\in B}\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q_J)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,P)$ is bijective. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to represent the preimage of $1_P$ by $s:P\to Q_J$ for some $J$. Its image is $rs$, where $r:Q_J\to P$ is the cocone component, so $rs=1_P$. This proves the retract assertion in Step 1. The construction in Steps 2-5 was for arbitrary $\mathcal C,\nu,\tau,G$ satisfying Step 1, so it may now be instantiated at different ranks.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: compactness/retract argument, made explicit rather than invoking an eventual-rank node.

proof.text:
For each $s$, choose an infinite regular accessibility witness $
u_s$ for $\mathcal A_s$ and its small generating family; for each $t$ choose a regular preservation witness $\alpha_t$ for $H_t$, as in the statement's definitions. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the disjoint union of sets of cardinalities $
u_s,\alpha_t$ and one additional set of cardinality $b$. It supplies an infinite regular $\eta_0$ strictly above all these cardinals, including when both families are empty. Put $ eta=(2^{\eta_0})^+$. By [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-successor-regular], $ eta$ is infinite regular. For $a< eta,d<
u_s$, we have $a\leq 2^{\eta_0}$, $d\leq\eta_0$, and $a^d\leq(2^{\eta_0})^{\eta_0}=2^{\eta_0}< eta$; the equality uses infinitude of $\eta_0$, and the inequality includes $d=0$. Apply the construction proved in Steps 1-5 to each $(\mathcal A_s,
u_s, eta)$; every $\mathcal A_s$ is $ eta$-accessible. Every $ eta$-filtered category is $\alpha_t$-filtered, so $H_t$ preserves these colimits.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: first common category rank above all original category and functor preservation ranks.

proof.text: Choose small families $G_s$ of $\beta$-presentable generators supplied by Step 6. For each $t$ and $g\in G_{a(t)}$, present $H_t(g)$ as a small $\beta$-filtered colimit of members of $G_{b(t)}$, indexed by $I_{t,g}$. Such a presentation exists by $\beta$-accessibility of the target. By [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound], applied to a set of size $\beta$ and the set of arrows of $I_{t,g}$, choose an infinite regular $\mu_{t,g}>\beta,|\operatorname{Mor}I_{t,g}|$. The objects of $G_{b(t)}$ are $\mu_{t,g}$-presentable by the filteredness inclusion used in Step 3. Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] to this particular presentation; it proves that $H_t(g)$ is $\mu_{t,g}$-presentable. Thus the presentability ranks of the images have been obtained without assuming cocompleteness or the locally-presentable object-rank lemma.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: bound the images of a small generator family, as in AR 2.19; presentability of each object is derived from its own accessible presentation.

proof.text: The set of pairs $(t,g)$ is small. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to sets of cardinalities $\mu_{t,g}$ and extra sets of cardinalities $\beta,b$, obtaining an infinite regular $\eta$ strictly larger than all of them. Set $\kappa=(2^\eta)^+$, infinite regular by [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-successor-regular]. For $a<\kappa,d<\beta$, the calculation $a^d\leq(2^\eta)^\eta=2^\eta<\kappa$ holds because $a\leq 2^\eta$, $d\leq\eta$ and $\eta$ is infinite. Instantiate Steps 1-5 with $(\nu,\tau,G)=(\beta,\kappa,G_s)$: every $\mathcal A_s$ is $\kappa$-accessible, and every $\kappa$-presentable $P\in\mathcal A_{a(t)}$ is a retract of some $Q=\operatorname{colim}_JF$ where $J$ is $\beta$-filtered with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows and $F$ takes values in $G_{a(t)}$. The functor $H_t$ preserves this colimit by Step 6. Each $H_t(F(j))$ is $\kappa$-presentable since $\mu_{t,F(j)}<\eta<\kappa$. Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] in $\mathcal A_{b(t)}$ to the colimit $H_t(Q)$; it is $\kappa$-presentable.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: second rank choice controlling generator images, and the small-colimit calculation for the image of the retract presentation.

proof.text: Write $s:P\to Q,r:Q\to P$ with $rs=1_P$. Functoriality gives $H_t(r)H_t(s)=1_{H_t(P)}$. Here is the presentability of a retract explicitly. Put $A=H_t(P),D=H_t(Q),u=H_t(s),v=H_t(r)$, so $vu=1_A$. On Hom sets put $i_Z(f)=fv$ and $p_Z(g)=gu$; then $p_Zi_Z=1$ and both maps commute with postcomposition. For any small $\kappa$-filtered diagram with colimit $Z$, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] induces the corresponding splitting on colimits of Hom sets. If $c_A,c_D$ are the Hom comparison maps, naturality says $c_Di=i_Zc_A$ and $c_Ap=p_Zc_D$. The map $c_D$ is bijective by Step 8. Then $p c_D^{-1}i_Z$ is inverse to $c_A$: its right composite with $c_A$ is $p i=1$, and its left composite is $p_Zi_Z=1$. Therefore $H_t(P)$ is $\kappa$-presentable.

source.place: Auxiliary ordinary uniformization: explicit retract comparison on Hom sets, proving strong accessibility without a new functor-eventual-rank node.

proof.text: Take $\lambda=\beta$. Step 6 gives existence and preservation of all small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. Since $\kappa>\eta>\beta$, every $\kappa$-filtered category is $\beta$-filtered, so the same preservation applies at $\kappa$. Step 8 gives $\kappa$-accessibility, and Step 9 gives preservation of $\kappa$-presentables. Also $b<\eta<\kappa$ and $\lambda<\kappa$, as required. This choice happens to make the categories $\lambda$-accessible, but the statement requires no such additional conclusion. If $S$ is empty then $T$ is empty because its functors have specified endpoints in $S$; the two cardinal choices and all vacuous conclusions still apply.
